article.title: Why a Stable Model Score Can Hide Population Drift
article.why: Learn why aggregate score stability does not rule out hidden drift.

paragraphs.en:
A machine-learning dashboard may show that the average prediction score has stayed almost unchanged for six months. That can feel reassuring. If the model’s mean score is stable, perhaps the population is stable too. Unfortunately, this conclusion can be wrong because important changes inside the population may cancel each other out.

Imagine a model that scores customers from 0 to 1. Younger customers gradually become less likely to convert, while older customers become more likely. If the two groups are similar in size, the overall mean score can remain at 0.24 even though the relationship between customer segments and the outcome has changed substantially. The stable average hides offsetting movement.

Population mix can create the same effect. Suppose high-value customers become a smaller share of the base while low-value customers become more active. Changes in segment proportions can offset changes in segment-level scores. Looking only at one aggregate number will not reveal whether the customer base, the model, or both are changing.

This is why drift monitoring should be decomposed. Teams can inspect feature distributions, missing-value rates, categorical shares, segment sizes, and score distributions over time. Metrics such as population stability index, distributional distance, or divergence measures can be useful, but the most important practice is often simple stratification: compare the same important customer groups across periods instead of relying only on the global average.

Another distinction is between data drift and concept drift. Data drift means the input distribution changes. Concept drift means the relationship between inputs and the target changes. A model can face concept drift even when input distributions look stable, and it can face input drift while maintaining acceptable performance. For that reason, production monitoring should eventually include outcome-based performance whenever labels arrive.

Calibration can also change selectively. The overall average predicted probability might remain correct while one segment becomes systematically overpredicted and another underpredicted. Aggregate calibration can therefore hide local miscalibration. Reliability plots by key segment or score band can reveal this pattern.

Operational changes add another layer. A new channel, campaign, eligibility rule, or source-system change can alter which customers enter scoring. That is not necessarily model failure, but it changes the population on which the model operates. Monitoring should therefore connect technical metrics with business events and data-pipeline changes.

A practical monitoring framework asks several questions at once. Has the score distribution changed? Have important feature distributions changed? Has the mix of customer segments changed? Are missing rates or category codes different? Has model performance changed once outcomes become available? Are the changes concentrated in a specific subgroup?

The broader lesson is that stability at the aggregate level is weak evidence of stability underneath. A mean score is a useful headline, but it should not be the only health check. In production machine learning, the most dangerous drift is often the kind that cancels out when everything is averaged together.

Threshold-based monitoring can also fail if it is too coarse. Suppose an alert is triggered only when the average score moves by more than five percent. Two large subgroups may move in opposite directions by ten percent each, leaving the total mean almost unchanged and producing no alert. Segment-aware monitoring or distribution-level metrics are more likely to catch this type of hidden movement.

Feature drift deserves similar care. A stable model score can be produced by unstable inputs if the model’s effects offset one another. For instance, one spending feature may rise while another engagement feature falls. The final prediction may stay similar because the model combines both. That is why monitoring only the output score cannot tell us whether the underlying data pipeline is healthy.

Teams should also distinguish expected seasonality from problematic drift. Holiday periods, bonus months, school calendars, or annual insurance renewals may create predictable changes. A good monitoring system compares current behavior with an appropriate historical baseline and records known business events. Otherwise, normal seasonality may create unnecessary alarms, while genuine structural changes may be dismissed as routine variation.
paragraphs.zh:
機器學習 dashboard 若顯示平均 prediction score 半年幾乎不變，看起來很安心，但平均穩定不代表 population 穩定。不同群體的變化可能互相抵消。

例如年輕顧客的 conversion propensity 下降、年長顧客上升，只要兩群規模相近，整體平均仍可能維持0.24。表面穩定，segment 與 outcome 的關係其實已改變。

Population mix 也可能造成同樣現象。高價值客比例下降、低價值客活躍度上升時，segment 比例與 segment-level score 的變化可能互相抵消。只看一個 aggregate number 無法判斷是顧客母體、模型，還是兩者都在變。

因此 drift monitoring 要拆解。除了 score distribution，也要看 feature distribution、missing rate、categorical share、segment size。PSI 或 distributional distance 可輔助，但最重要的常是 stratification：固定重要群體後跨期比較。

Data drift 指 input distribution 改變；concept drift 指 input 與 target 的關係改變。即使 input 看似穩定也可能 concept drift，因此 label 回來後仍要監控 outcome-based performance。

Calibration 也可能局部惡化：整體平均預測率正確，但某 segment 系統性 overpredict、另一群 underpredict。應看 segment 或 score band 的 reliability。

新 channel、campaign、eligibility rule、source-system 變更都可能改變誰被送進模型，未必是 model failure，卻會改變 operating population。Technical metric 要和 business event、pipeline change 一起解讀。

實務監控應同時問：score 分布變了嗎？重要 feature 變了嗎？segment mix 變了嗎？missing/category code 變了嗎？label 回來後 performance 變了嗎？是否集中在特定 subgroup？

Aggregate stability 只是很弱的健康證據。Mean score 可以當 headline，但不能是唯一 health check。最危險的 drift 常常正是被平均抵消掉的那一種。

如果 alert 只看平均 score 變動超過5%，兩個大 subgroup 各自正負10%的變化可能完全不觸發警報。Segment-aware 或 distribution-level monitoring 更容易抓到隱藏變化。

Feature drift 也一樣。某 spending feature 上升、某 engagement feature 下降時，model output 可能剛好維持不變，所以只看 output 無法知道底層 data pipeline 是否健康。

另外要區分 seasonality 與真正 drift。假期、bonus 月、學期、年度續約都可能帶來預期變化，因此監控應搭配適當 historical baseline 與 business event 紀錄。
paragraphs.ja:
machine-learning dashboardで平均prediction scoreが半年ほぼ同じでも、populationが安定しているとは限りません。segmentごとの変化が相殺される可能性があります。

例えば若年層のconversion propensityが低下し、高年層が上昇しても、両者の規模が近ければoverall meanは0.24のままです。平均は安定していてもsegmentとoutcomeの関係は変わっています。

population mixでも同じです。高価値顧客の比率低下と低価値層の活性化が重なると、segment比率とsegment-level scoreの変化が打ち消し合います。aggregate numberだけでは顧客基盤、model、両方のどれが変わったか分かりません。

そのためdrift monitoringは分解して行います。feature distribution、missing率、category構成、segment size、score distributionを期間別に確認します。PSIなども有効ですが、重要なのは同じ主要segmentを時系列比較するstratificationです。

data driftはinput distributionの変化、concept driftはinputとtargetの関係変化です。inputが安定して見えてもconcept driftは起こり得るため、label取得後はoutcome-based performanceも確認します。

calibrationもsegment別に崩れることがあります。全体平均は合っていても、一方でoverprediction、他方でunderpredictionが起きればaggregate calibrationは問題を隠します。

新channel、campaign、eligibility rule、source-system変更はscoring対象populationを変えます。model failureとは限りませんが、technical metricとbusiness eventを結び付ける必要があります。

実務ではscore distribution、feature distribution、segment mix、missing/category code、label取得後performance、特定subgroupへの集中を同時に確認します。

aggregate levelの安定は弱い証拠です。mean scoreはheadlineとして有用でも唯一のhealth checkにはできません。平均化で相殺されるdriftほど見逃しやすいからです。

平均scoreが5％動いたときだけalertする設計では、二つの大segmentが逆方向に10％動いても警報が出ません。segment-aware monitoringが必要です。

feature driftも同様で、利用額feature上昇とengagement feature低下がmodel内で相殺されればoutputは安定します。outputだけでdata pipelineの健全性は判断できません。

holiday、bonus月、学校calendar、更新時期などのseasonalityも区別し、適切なhistorical baselineとbusiness event記録を使うべきです。

vocabulary.usage: Use stratification to reveal hidden changes.
Concept drift changes the input-target relationship.
Use reliability plots by score band.
Aggregate stability can hide subgroup drift.
Opposite movements can offset each other.

business.term: A stable mean score is not proof of a stable population.
business.explanation: 提醒 production monitoring 不能只看平均分數。

business.term: Monitor the distribution and the segments behind the headline metric.
business.explanation: 建議把 global metric 拆到群體與分布。

sources: Production ML monitoring, data drift, concept drift, calibration, and segmented distribution analysis.
